provenance.source: docs/lsc-grammar (DBLSC corpus) — chapters ch02-estructura-dblsc.md, ch03-apendice-gramatical.md, ch08-discurso-lsc-articulo.md
provenance.note: Rules are distilled from what the chapters actually state; the two spec-mandated behaviors (drop copula, time-fronting) are standard LSC structure the chapters assume (ch08 example 'Ayer María le dijo…' opens with the time sign; ch02 forbids word-by-word translation). Lookup precedence in the gloss mapper is: vocabulary match first, then rules — so lexical signs such as SI (afirmación) or PARA-QUE (pregunta) are never dropped even when their lemmas appear in a drop category.

rules.drop-copula: Spanish copula has no lexical sign in LSC; ch02 anti-pattern: 'Tratar la glosa como traducción literal palabra por palabra del español a la LSC'.
rules.drop-connectors: ch08: 'sectores, sucedáneos, depictions y body shifting construyen cohesión y punto de vista donde el español usa pronombres y conectores' — connectors collapse into spatial/discourse structure.
rules.drop-intensifiers: ch03 §2.b: intensity is graded in sign channels (space, speed, bimanualism), 'no "muy" copiado' — intensifiers are never lexicalized as copied adverbs.
rules.drop-articles: ch08 anti-pattern: 'Traducir artículo por artículo del español a señas' — LSC has no article system; referents live in sectors.
rules.drop-prepositions: ch03 §2.a: spatial trajectory (arriba/abajo/lejos/cerca) 'se expresa como parte de la seña, no como palabra añadida' — spatial prepositions fold into verb movement.
rules.time-front: ch08 worked example fronts 'Ayer' before the topic; ch03 §2.d temporal sector. LSC time-topic-comment: time expressions sign first.
rules.reorder: ch08 §5: 'la sintaxis del español se colapsa en el mapa espacial' and one verb can carry a whole Spanish sentence. Approximated for the MVP as verb-final order; the chapters frame it as spatial collapse, not a fixed surface order, so this rule is the least literal of the set.
